newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan central bank gets wide new powers.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan central bank gets wide new powers.

text.p: State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) governor Muhammad Yaqub said on Wednesday that three new ordinances had given the central bank sweeping new powers.
Yaqub told a news conference that the ordinances, issued on Tuesday, had made the bank truly autonomous, giving it authority to formulate and monitor monetary and credit policy.
It could also formulate and review rules and regulations of the banking system and take drastic action against defaulters.

The SBP could act to prevent potential losses to banks, such as those arising from the so-called Yellow Cab scheme promoted by a previous government led by Nawaz Sharif to sell imported duty-free cars to unemployed people on easy terms, he said.
"If the State Bank wants to create a firewall, it can," Yaqub said. "If the State Bank does not want a Yellow Cab scheme, there would be no Yellow Cab scheme."

The SBP would frame monetary and fiscal policies, and enforce them, he said. The government would not be able to exceed its set credit line with the central bank. If it required more funds it would have to raise them from commercial banks.
"If and when this gets implemented, this will change the history of this country," Yaqub said.
The ordinances, promulgated by President Farooq Leghari, are a key component of banking sector reforms which the caretaker government hopes will be supported by a World Bank loan.
He said there would be a transitional period and the SBP would coordinate with the government on its budget needs, while inflation and growth targets would be set nationally.
"The SBP as a regulatory agency will develop soundness of the banking system," he said. "We want to live by the law. We want to introduce transparency. Violators would be punished."
Yaqub said all Pakistanis should help to fight corruption. "The garbage cannot be cleared in one day," he said.
He said the managements of state-run banks would be improved before their privatisation. "Appointments will be on professional basis and there will be no political appointments."
